Thank you for your interest in National University!

 National University, one of the largest private nonprofit universities in the United States, is committed to your success through our Whole Human Education approach. 


Flexible Learning on Your Terms

National University's flexible four and eight-week online courses allow you to focus on one class at a time. With unlimited free tutoring, individual coaching, and a dedicated writing center, we provide the support you need to excel. NU accepts and reviews applications year-round, so you can start your classes as soon as next month, depending on your program of study and location of choice. To learn more about applying, visit our Admissions page or call (855) 355-6288. 

 

Additional Resources

·      NU Course Equivalency Site: See how your other previous courses or exams will transfer to NU.

·      ADT Degrees: Explore scholarship and degree pathways for CCC students with ADT degrees.

·      Financial Aid: Discover how our Financial Aid team can help you secure the necessary resources.

·      NU Catalog: For detailed policies and more information.

This articulation agreement outlines the preparatory courses required in the major, based on quarter credit hours. National University courses are listed on the left, with their approved (articulated) transfer equivalents on the right. General education and campus requirements for all bachelor’s degrees are detailed in separate agreements, which can be accessed in ASSIST by selecting “General Education/Breadth” on the left panel.  Additionally, NU accepts CSU GE Breadth, IGETC, and Cal-GETC certification to fulfill its GE requirements, except for at least one upper-division GE elective. 


NU allows a maximum of 12 semester units (18 quarter units) of vocational/technical coursework. Transfer courses noted with \"Limits Apply to Non-CSU Transferable Courses\" will count toward this limit.


For more information on this and all degrees at National University, see Program Finder.

 

Changes to this Agreement

Major requirements are subject to change. Newly articulated courses are added on a rolling basis, and the articulation status of some courses may be revised or discontinued. For the most current information, please visit ASSIST every quarter and regularly consult with an academic counselor at NU or your institution.

As such, they do not prepare students to work as paralegals. In addition, pre-law programs are neither evaluated nor approved by the American Bar Association and, thus, the NU Pre-Law Studies program is not so approved.

Students who are currently enrolled in the Bachelor of Arts in Pre-Law Studies degree program have the option to participate in the 3 + 3 Accelerated BA/JD Pathway. If accepted to JFK School of Law, the student would replace their upper-division electives (36 quarter units) in the bachelor’s program with the first year of the Juris Doctor program (24 semester units). The following is the program sequence for the 3 + 3 Accelerated BA in Pre-Law Studies/JD Pathway: LAW 112A, LAW 115A, LAW 117A, LAW120, LAW 112B, LAW 115B, LAW 117B, and LAW 318. This pathway allows students to complete their undergraduate pre-law degree and Juris Doctorate in an expedited time frame.


Students accepted into the 3 + 3 Accelerated BA/JD Pathway would replace their upper-division electives (36 quarter units) in the bachelor’s program with the first year of the Juris Doctor program (24 semester units). Pending meeting the requirements of, and receiving grades acceptable in, the JD program*, the student would graduate with a Bachelor of Arts in Pre-Law Studies in their last undergraduate year, having already completed one year in the Juris Doctor program. The student would then continue in the Juris Doctor program for two more years toward the successful completion of that degree. Students completing the 3 + 3 Accelerated BA/ JD Pathway qualify to sit for the California Bar Exam.


To support a cohesive pathway to a Juris Doctorate degree, National University’s Bachelor of Arts in Pre-Law Studies undergraduate students who successfully meet all requirements of admission to the JFK School of Law at National University and have opted to participate in the 3 + 3 program will be considered preferred candidates for admission to the JFK School of Law at National University’s JD program.


3 + 3 Accelerated BA/JD Pathway students would need to have their completed undergraduate credits verified before applying to the JFK School of Law. Acceptance to the JD program is not guaranteed. Applicants will be evaluated for eligibility and readiness through the Juris Doctor application process
